This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use distancing (a form of cognitive reappraisal) to down-regulate emotion while viewing visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., DISTANCING > negative-VIEW; SPATIAL/TEMPORAL/OBJECTIVE > negative-VIEW) and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with clusterwise inference and peak coordinates reported. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (increase/decrease) during presentation of visual stimuli (static face photographs). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation to view ([increase + decrease] > view) and describes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and identified peak regions (reported in tables). The sample includes both patients with lifetime MDD and matched healthy controls with results reported across/within groups. These features satisfy all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I5–I11). The full text provided contains methods, results, and tables/figures described, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is a randomized, placebo-controlled, task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (distraction vs. passive viewing) using visual IAPS pictures, reports within-task contrasts (distract-negative > attend-negative; attend-negative > attend-neutral), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI peak coordinates and statistical maps. Both PTSD patients and trauma-exposed controls are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply: the paper is empirical, reports whole-brain activation maps (not ROI-only), includes within-task effects, and is not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation instruction. Full text appears complete.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of instructed cognitive reappraisal using visual IAPS images in older adults and reports within-task regulation contrasts, the reported analyses are ROI-based only. The methods and results describe a priori ROI GLM contrasts and ROI tables; no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space are reported. This means the study reports only ROI results without an accompanying whole-brain analysis, which meets exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation — cognitive reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli — IAPS images), I8 (sample allowed — older adults), I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts). Inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps with peak coordinates) is not met. Therefore the study must be excluded under E4.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and distraction) while presenting visual IAPS pictures to healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion induction and regulation (e.g., view NEG – view NEU; view NEG – distract; view NEG – reappraise) and provides peak coordinates in MNI space. The manuscript also states that complementary exploratory whole-brain analyses (Supplementary Table 1) are provided, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (coordinates reported in text/tables/supplement). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, non-empirical, connectivity-only analyses) apply.

This article meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is an empirical, task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal: “decrease negative”) during presentation of stimuli (I6). Stimuli were visual static images (negative and neutral pictures) (I7). The sample includes clinical (female adolescents with conduct disorder) and typically developing control groups reported separately (I8). Analyses report within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (decrease negative > look negative) and unregulated viewing contrasts (look negative > look neutral) (I9). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were conducted and whole-brain familywise-error-corrected results are reported (cluster-level FWE and references to peak/cluster reports), satisfying the whole-brain reporting requirement (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, within-group effects are reported). Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed cognitive reappraisal using visual IAPS images in a clinical sample and reports the within-task contrast ReappNeg > LookNeg (meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9). However, the paper reports results based on ROI-extracted beta weights (AAL-based ROIs) and PCA of those ROIs rather than presenting a group-level whole-brain, voxelwise activation map with peak coordinates in standard space. No whole-brain peak coordinates or voxelwise tables/figures are provided, so it lacks the required whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (I10 not met). This places the study into exclusion category E4 (only ROI-based results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal/distancing as an emotion regulation strategy during presentation of visual stimuli (I6,I7). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Decrease > Look-Negative; Look-Negative > Look-Neutral) used for analyses (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates and family-wise-error correction (P < .05 FWE) (I10), and these whole-brain results and coordinates are described in the text/tables (I11). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; within-group effects reported; not an empathy-only perspective task).

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs view) using visual stimuli (IAPS images) in adults with ADHD and matched healthy controls. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > negative view; negative view > neutral view) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with corrected cluster/voxelwise results and anatomical labels. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and reports within-group task effects. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion-regulation (cognitive reappraisal) paradigm with visual picture stimuli. The paper reports within-task contrasts of interest (Regulate > Maintain and Maintain > Observe), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space, and provides results for both an obese patient group and healthy controls. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-visual stimuli, non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it fails inclusion criterion I7: the emotional stimuli were participant-generated written sentences/negative self-beliefs (word/sentence stimuli) rather than visual images or film, and the review excludes studies that regulate responses to word/sentence stimuli. Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: reappraisal and acceptance), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), and I11 (results reported with coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (visual stimuli requirement). Exclusion criteria applied: none (E3–E7 not triggered). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study with instructed cognitive reappraisal of visual (video) stimuli and reports results separately for SAD patients and healthy controls (meets I5, I6, I7, I8). However, the paper presents ROI-based network (DEPNA) connectivity analyses and does not report any group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-activation maps with peak coordinates in standard space. Thus it fails the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results (I10 not met). Because the imaging results are reported only as ROI/seed-based connectivity (DEPNA) without accompanying whole-brain activation maps, this study meets exclusion criteria E4 and E5 (ROI-only/partial-coverage/connectivity-only reporting). Also, the paper does not provide the conventional within-task whole-brain activation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look) as voxelwise maps (I9 not satisfied for whole-brain contrast reporting). Therefore it should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation using visual IAPS stimuli (MAINTAIN vs SUPPRESS) in bipolar and healthy participants, and it reports within-task connectivity contrasts. However, the paper reports only ROI-based connectivity and graph-theory/Network-Based Statistic results derived from low-frequency BOLD correlations and does not present any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps with peak coordinates in standard space. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (connectivity-only analyses without a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation via reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli — IAPS images), I8 (sample criteria satisfied), I9 (within-task contrasts MAINTAIN vs SUPPRESS reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map with coordinates reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion provided).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (attend vs. reappraise) using visual stimuli (IAPS and alcohol images). Participant groups include AUD patients and healthy controls with group-specific analyses. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > attend; attend emotion > attend neutral) and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses reported at whole-brain FWE-corrected thresholds. The manuscript contains full introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation that instructs cognitive reappraisal (an emotion regulation strategy) using visual stimuli (IAPS images). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise > Look-Negative) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak MNI coordinates and FWE correction. The sample (clinical patients with GAD, SAD, MDD) is acceptable per inclusion criteria, and the full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-task contrasts are reported. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs attend). Emotional stimuli were visual (IAPS and validated alcohol images). The sample includes alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls with results reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > attend per emotion; attend emotion > attend neutral) and whole-brain second-level voxelwise analyses with standard-space coordinates and corrected thresholds. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal to downregulate emotions (meets I5 and I6). Emotional stimuli were visual pictures (neutral, fear, OCD-related) (I7). Participant groups include OCD patients and unrelated healthy controls with separate reporting, and unaffected siblings (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts (fear regulate > attend; OCD regulate > attend; fear > neutral; OCD > neutral) and within-group regulation effects (I9). The manuscript references and presents whole-brain analyses and supplemental whole-brain results with MNI coordinates (tables and supplement), satisfying the requirement for group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no review-only, ROI-only, or connectivity-only reporting; within-group effects are reported; not an empathy/perspective-only task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This task-based fMRI study uses visual (face) stimuli and reports the unregulated contrast (match faces vs. match shapes) and whole-brain subject-specific contrast maps, and includes healthy adult participants and behavioral measures of perceived stress and inattention. However, the fMRI task did NOT instruct an emotion regulation strategy (implicit reappraisal was inferred rather than instructed), so it fails inclusion criterion I6. Additionally, the paper does not report a group-level, voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates in standard space (no whole-brain peak coordinates/tables are provided in the main text), so it fails I10. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample), I9 (reports an unregulated viewing contrast). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed regulation), I10 (no group-level whole-brain map with coordinates). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (I5, I6). Stimuli were visual IAPS pictures (static images) (I7). The sample includes clinical groups (BD, SZ) and healthy controls with results reported separately (I8). The analyses include within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraise > attend-negative; attend-negative > attend-neutral) (I9). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses were performed (3dMVM in AFNI) with cluster correction and reported cluster results (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is empirical with original fMRI data (not E3), reports whole-brain results (not only ROI; not E4), is not only connectivity/resting-state (not E5), includes within-task effects (not E6), and is not an empathy/perspective task without regulation instruction (not E7). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

Excluded because the report presents task-based seed/PPI connectivity and ROI-based connectivity analyses without reporting any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or peak coordinates. This violates exclusion criterion E5. The study does meet several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (explicit instructed emotion regulation: reappraisal and acceptance), I7 (visual stimuli: emotional faces and video clips), I8 (clinical sample with SAD), and I9 (within-task contrasts such as affect label > gender label, reappraisal > passive viewing, acceptance > passive viewing). However, it does NOT meet I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates is reported). The full text appears complete. Confidence in this decision is high.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal and imagery) during viewing of visual IAPS pictures. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (reappraise > maintain; change image > maintain; maintain > just look), includes whole-brain group-level analyses with peak MNI coordinates (tables/figures), and provides complete methods, results, and discussion. Sample and analyses meet inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that presents visual emotional stimuli (film clips) and reports within-task contrasts of emotion-evoking (EE) vs emotion-neutral (EN) conditions (EE−EN) using group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported significant clusters. The sample is acceptable (healthy adult groups). Although the task did not instruct an explicit emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal), the meta-analysis objective includes studies that involve unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., emotion > neutral), which this study provides. Full text includes introduction, methods (fMRI acquisition and analysis), results (behavioral, HRV, whole-brain contrasts) and discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for inclusion as an unregulated visual emotion-viewing fMRI study reporting whole-brain activation maps.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (self-focused distancing) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures) in healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Decrease > LookNeg) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and tables/figures. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, reports whole-brain results, includes within-group task effects, not an empathy study without regulation). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study with healthy adult participants using visual stimuli (offers and written messages), reporting within-task contrasts (e.g., unfair > fair) and whole-brain group-level analyses with coordinates. However, it does not meet the critical requirement that an emotion regulation strategy was instructed: participants performed an anger-infused Ultimatum Game without instructions to up- or down-regulate their emotions (implicit/automatic regulation only). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded from the review.

Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (within-task contrasts such as unfair > fair), I10 (whole-brain group-level analysis), I11 (reporting coordinates/tables). 
Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy).
Exclusion IDs met: None ([])

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of explicit emotion regulation using instructed strategies (reappraisal and response modulation) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., regulate > maintain, increase > decrease) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI peak coordinates for amygdala and PFC clusters. The sample (healthy young adults) is eligible and the full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not non-empirical, and not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This paper is a coordinate-based meta-analysis (ALE) aggregating peak coordinates from previously published fMRI studies rather than reporting original, primary task-based fMRI data. Exclusion criterion met: E3 (non-empirical paper / meta-analysis without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none (no I5–I11 are satisfied for this paper as an original empirical report). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a primary task-based fMRI study), I6 (does not itself instruct participants in an emotion-regulation fMRI task), I7 (does not present original visual-stimulus task data), I8 (does not report original participant sample results), I9 (does not report within-task contrasts from original data), I10/I11 (does not provide original group-level whole-brain statistical maps as primary empirical results; it compiles coordinates from other studies). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (Reappraise vs Maintain) using visual stimuli (IAPS negative scenes; faces). The sample is healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Reappraise>Maintain) and other within-task contrasts (Surprise>Neutral, Fear>Neutral), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and peak coordinates (ROI coordinates and cluster results described). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment (Experiment 3) in which participants were instructed to cognitively reappraise visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images) with explicit Increase/Maintain/Decrease instructions. It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Increase > Maintain, Decrease > Maintain), whole-brain group-level activation results with peak coordinates and corrected thresholds, and provides full methods and results. Participant sample is healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal during viewing of visual stimuli (IAPS), includes both bipolar patients and healthy controls reported separately, and reports within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraising > attending-negative). Group-level whole-brain GLM analyses are described with cluster- and voxelwise thresholds and activation coordinate tables (Tables S3/S4), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Although the paper also includes effective connectivity (DCM) analyses, whole-brain task activation maps and contrasts relevant to emotion regulation are present. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the record is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed cognitive reappraisal (I6) using visual IAPS images (I7) in a healthy adult sample (I8) and reports a within-task contrast (ReappNeg vs LookNeg) (I9). However, the full text presents analyses based on ROI-extracted beta weights (AAL ROIs) submitted to PCA and discriminant analysis, and does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps with peak coordinates in standard space (no tables/figures of whole-brain peaks or coordinates are provided). Therefore it appears to report ONLY ROI-based results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis, which meets exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise map with coordinates). Exclusion criteria met: E4. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (explicit suppression) and uses priming for implicit suppression during viewing of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and other images). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing suppression runs to baseline (e.g., EXP vs BASEEXP), Dm (subsequent memory) contrasts, group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses with tables/clusters and ROI analyses, and peak coordinates. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) and also includes an attentional-control implicit regulation task. Stimuli are visual (IAPS images and facial photographs). The sample is healthy adults. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise > Look-Negative; Threat Low > Threat High) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and FWE correction. Results and methods are fully reported in the main text. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; reports within-group task effects; not an empathy/perspective-taking-only study). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (self-focused increase and decrease) during presentation of visual stimuli (anger facial photographs). The paper reports behavioral and neural within-task contrasts (e.g., increase > view-angry, decrease > view-angry, view-angry > view-neutral), provides whole-brain group-level results with anatomical localization and tables/figures in standard space, and reports patient and healthy control groups separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition and analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review and is appropriate for meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual facial stimuli and reports unregulated viewing contrasts, but it does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy during scanning (I6 not met). The paper uses an ROI-focused analysis (family-wise error within predefined ROIs) and presents ROI-derived coordinates rather than reporting a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map, so it lacks qualifying whole-brain results (I10 not met) and thus meets exclusion criterion E4. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study cannot be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (distancing, a form of cognitive reappraisal) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and Emopics images). The sample includes anorexia nervosa patients and matched healthy controls with group-level results reported separately. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., positive watch > positive distance, positive watch > neutral) and explicitly states that whole-brain analyses were performed and corrected (results reported in main/supplementary tables and figures). All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply (e.g., the study does not report only ROI/small-volume results nor only connectivity analyses). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it does not meet two required inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis: I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy) and I7 (emotional stimuli are visual images/film). Instead, the fMRI tasks directed participants to engage in rumination (provocation-focused, self-focused, neutral-focused), which is not an instructed regulation strategy such as reappraisal/acceptance, and the emotional stimuli/feedback and prompts were presented as written text (word/sentence stimuli). The study does meet several other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible sample with group results), I9 (reports within-task contrasts such as feedback > pre-feedback baseline and provocation-focus > neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates), and I11 (coordinates/whole-brain results reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded for failure to satisfy I6 and I7.

This full-text meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly instructs emotion regulation strategies including cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression (I6). Emotional stimuli were visual static images from the IAPS (I7). The sample includes a clinical group (schizophrenia) and healthy controls, with task results reported for patient group (I8). The analyses report within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (reappraise > attend negative; suppress > attend negative) (I9). Whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed and reported (cluster-level FWE correction), with results presented in text/figures/tables consistent with standard MNI coordinates (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper reports whole-brain task activation maps (not only ROI or connectivity-only results). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore include in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed cognitive reappraisal via distancing to downregulate emotion (meets I5,I6). Stimuli were visual pictures (negative, positive, neutral), meeting I7. Sample includes acute AN patients and matched healthy controls with group results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation and viewing (negative watch > neutral; negative watch > negative distance; negative watch < negative distance) (I9). Group-level voxelwise analyses and whole-brain/exploratory results with peak coordinates are reported (figures/Supplementary, coordinate peaks in text), satisfying I10 and I11. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion; no exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group task effects, not an empathy task). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (‘‘decrease’’ vs ‘‘look’’) using visual IAPS images, satisfying the emotion-regulation task and stimulus requirements. The sample (PTSD patients with a randomized waiting-list control) is acceptable and group results are reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (decrease > look) and provides voxel-wise, whole-brain longitudinal analyses (with supplemental tables/figures of coordinates), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; includes whole-brain results beyond ROIs; reports within-group task effects in addition to interactions). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets I5–I11 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis focused on instructed emotion regulation to visual stimuli.

Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study reports only resting-state/effective connectivity analyses without any task-evoked whole-brain activation contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample: participant groups reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study), I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation task; no cognitive reappraisal or other regulation instruction), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli—resting-state with eyes closed), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise maps reported). The article is a complete full-text report of a resting-state sDCM connectivity study and thus does not address the meta-analysis objective of task-based emotion regulation with visual stimuli. Full text appears complete for screening purposes (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Full text reports an empirical task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (DECREASE vs LOOK) during presentation of visual IAPS images (static pictures). Sample and methods are appropriate; within-task regulation contrasts (decrease-negative > look-negative) and unregulated viewing contrasts (look-negative > look-neutral) are reported. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FWE-corrected maps and peak coordinates cited). Full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This full-text fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) that instructs emotion regulation strategies including cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) and distraction (I6). Emotional stimuli are visual static pictures (IAPS and internet images) (I7). The sample (healthy adult females) is an eligible participant group (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation and unregulated viewing (e.g., down-regulation > look, up-regulation > look, look aversive > look neutral) (I9). Group-level whole-brain analyses were conducted and reported (exploratory whole-brain results and MNI coordinates are provided for multiple contrasts), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I10). Results and whole-brain/ROI findings are described in text and tables/supplements (I11). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion-regulation task (affect labeling: Label > Observe contrasts) with visual stimuli (faces). The paper reports within-task contrasts for negative and positive emotion regulation (NegLabel > NegObserve), conducts whole-brain voxelwise analyses (PPI whole-brain regressions and whole-brain activation regressions) with cluster correction and reports cluster results/coordinates (tables/figures), and includes an eligible sample (adolescent participants). Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (face images) with group-level whole-brain analyses and reported peak coordinates, it does not test an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (criterion I6). The task is affect labeling (label the emotion) rather than an instruction to regulate (e.g., reappraise, accept, distance, or otherwise up-/down-regulate emotion). The main reported contrast (affect label > gender label) is not an instructed regulation > look contrast nor a passive viewing (emotion > baseline) contrast as specified in I9. Therefore it fails the key eligibility requirements for this review (I6 and I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I10, I11. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I9. Full text appears complete.

Full-text reports a task-based fMRI study using instructed cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs Look conditions) with visual IAPS images, single-trial/block contrasts (Look-Negative>Look-Neutral; Reappraise>Look-Neutral), and a whole-brain voxelwise group-level analysis reporting MNI peak coordinates and cluster-corrected results. The sample includes a clinical GAD group and healthy controls with results reported separately. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; therefore complete. Meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an empirical task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs a cognitive emotion regulation strategy (distancing reappraisal) during stimulus presentation (I6). The emotional stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7). The sample includes a participant group (male marijuana users) with matched controls and reports group-level results (I8). This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study that directly examines instructed emotion regulation (reappraise > look) and uninstructed viewing (look negative > look neutral) using visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts (reappraise > look; look negative > look neutral) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and thresholding, and presents coordinate-based results. Sample is healthy adults. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper meets several inclusion criteria (I5: task-based fMRI; I6: instructed emotion regulation with reappraisal and selective attention; I7: visual stimuli — 40 s negative film clips; I8: acceptable sample including younger and older adults; I9: reports within-task contrasts related to regulation, here as PPI contrasts such as reappraisal > passive viewing and reappraisal > selective attention). However, it violates key requirements: the article reports only seed-based functional connectivity (PPI) analyses conducted within an a priori PFC/amygdala mask and does not present a group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates in standard space (I10 not met). Therefore exclusion criteria E5 (reports ONLY seed-based/effective connectivity without a whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (reports only ROI/small-volume-masked results with no whole-brain analysis) apply. Note: the authors state that neural activity contrasts were reported previously (Allard & Kensinger, 2014), but those whole-brain activation results are not presented in this full text. Full text appears complete for this paper. Given E4 and E5, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use emotion regulation strategies (Detachment, Reinterpretation, Distraction, Expressive Suppression) while viewing visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., ‘Regulate Negative’ > ‘Permit Negative’ and vice versa), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and FWE-corrected results, and presents full methods, results, and discussion. Sample (healthy adults) is eligible. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports an original, task-based fMRI experiment using an instructed emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). Participants include clinical (PTSD) and combat-exposed control groups with group-level analyses reported separately. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise > Maintain) and unregulated viewing contrasts (Maintain > Look), and provides whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates and corrected thresholds. The manuscript includes complete methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed emotion regulation (look, increase, decrease) using cognitive reappraisal strategies (I6). Stimuli were visual (IAPS and in-house disgusting images) (I7). The sample includes children/adolescents with ASD and TD controls (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (decrease-gross vs. look-gross; increase-gross vs. look-gross) (I9). It performed group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses and references coordinate tables/figures (Table S2, figures) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical with original fMRI task activation maps (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only), and includes within-group task effects. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise > look contrasts) and reports within-task contrasts. Stimuli include visual faces (fearful and neutral) used during the instruction/regulation period; although top-down generation used sentences as background, the regulated stimulus during instruction is a visual face, so the study meets the visual-stimuli requirement. The sample (healthy adult women) is acceptable. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and tables/figures of activations and coordinates. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies I5–I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs a cognitive reappraisal (Regulate) strategy versus a control (Attend) during a sequential investment task. The stimuli are visual market displays presented on-screen and evoke emotional/regret responses related to financial decisions. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing Regulate and Attend and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with reported coordinates (MNI) and thresholding, plus tables in Supporting Information. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

Study 2 reports a task-based fMRI experiment using instructed cognitive reappraisal ("CHANGE" vs "LOOK") during presentation of visual IAPS images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (look negative > look neutral; decrease negative > look negative) and group-level whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates reported (Table 5). Participant groups (DSH and depression control) are reported separately. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study should be excluded because the emotional stimuli being regulated are non-visual (anticipation of somatosensory pain via intraepidermal electrical stimulation), which fails inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be VISUAL). The study does meet multiple inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive reappraisal during anticipation), I8 (eligible sample: healthy participants reported separately), I9 (reports within-task contrasts related to regulation, e.g., regulation vs. anxiety), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), and I11 (results/coordinates described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded due to not meeting I7 (non-visual regulated stimuli).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in which children (8–12 yrs) were instructed to use a cognitive reappraisal strategy (“MAKE-POSITIVE”) while viewing visual sad images (IAPS and child-appropriate photos). The paper reports within-task contrasts (reappraise sad vs. view sad; view sad vs. view neutral) and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with corrected thresholds) as well as ROI analyses. Core article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to use self-focused cognitive reappraisal (distancing, increase, decrease) while viewing visual IAPS images. It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (DistA > PermA; IncA > PermA) and an unregulated viewing contrast (PermA > PermN). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-level correction and coordinate tables. The sample includes a clinical group (SAD) and matched controls with separate group analyses. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructed participants to voluntarily generate (up-regulate) a positive mood while viewing visual stimuli (happy facial expressions) and using autobiographical memory. It reports within-task analyses using activation during the happy mood induction blocks (regression of PANAS change with brain activation), group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with MNI peak coordinates and cluster tables, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. All inclusion criteria relevant to the review are met (task-based fMRI, instructed regulation/up-regulation during visual stimuli, visual stimuli used, eligible sample, within-task activation/contrast analyses, and whole-brain coordinate reporting). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal: “Decrease” vs. “Look”), with visual stimuli (negative and neutral images). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Regulate Negative vs. Look Negative) and also whole-brain group-level analyses (whole-brain effects and tables/figures reported, with coordinates in supplements). Sample and analyses meet inclusion requirements. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study fits the meta-analysis objective and inclusion criteria.

This study meets several inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), explicitly instructs emotion regulation strategies including cognitive reappraisal and selective attention (I6), uses visual emotional stimuli in the form of film/video clips (I7), includes an eligible sample of younger and older adults (I8), and reports within-task contrasts comparing regulation and passive viewing (I9). However, all reported activation analyses were conducted within an explicit amygdala–PFC mask (region-limited search space), and the paper does not present a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation analysis with peak coordinates in standard space. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I10) and appears to report only region-of-interest / small-volume–restricted results, triggering exclusion criterion E4. Full text appears complete. Because I10 is not met and E4 applies, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (volitional emotion regulation) using visual IAPS pictures. It reports within-task contrasts comparing Reappraise versus Maintain and includes whole-brain group-level voxelwise activation analyses (activation results and tables of coordinates) and supplementary tables/figures. All relevant inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplementary materials).

Full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were explicitly instructed to use cognitive reappraisal (Reapp Neg) versus look (Look Neg/Look Neu) to regulate responses to visual stimuli (IAPS images). The study provides within-task contrasts (Reapp Neg vs Look Neg), whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI peak coordinates and cluster thresholds, and reports group-level results. Sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an original, task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion-regulation manipulation (guided attentional distraction vs evaluation) with visual, static OCD-relevant and aversive images. The paper reports within-task contrasts (evaluation > distraction; OCD-relevant > neutral/aversive) and group-level, whole-brain analyses (with ROI follow-up), with results presented in figures and supplementary tables. Both patient and matched healthy control groups are reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group task effects). Full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so it is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of instructed regulation (visual stimuli) and is included.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (and affect labeling) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Label > Observe, Reappraise > Observe, Label > Reappraise, etc.) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (SPM5, MNI coordinates). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text reports a task-based fMRI experiment instructing emotion regulation (reappraisal and distraction) using visual IAPS pictures in healthy high-risk and control groups. It provides within-task contrasts (view negative > neutral; reappraisal negative > view negative; distraction positive > view positive) from second-level random-effects analyses and gives peak coordinates in MNI space for group-level contrasts. The full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is available. Although ROI-based correction was used, group-level voxelwise contrasts with MNI coordinates are reported, satisfying the whole-brain coordinate reporting requirement for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly used a cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation) paradigm with instructed regulation (Suppress/reappraise) and a passive Observe condition. Emotional stimuli were visual IAPS pictures. The paper reports within-task contrasts of interest (Maintain>Observe and Suppress>Maintain) and describes group-level whole-brain voxel-wise analyses with correction and supplementary tables for full results/coordinates. The sample includes cocaine-dependent groups and a healthy control group with group results reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion; supplementary tables are referenced but their absence does not render the main text incomplete.

This is a task-based (event-related) fMRI study that explicitly instructed emotion-regulation strategies (reappraisal and expressive suppression) during an anticipation (cue) and stimulus (target) period. Visual stimuli were used (IAPS negative images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Target Reappraisal > Target Appraise, Cue Suppression > Cue Reappraisal) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and MNI coordinates in tables. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because it does NOT meet I6: the fMRI task is affect labeling, an incidental/implicit process, not an instructed emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal, distancing, acceptance). Although labeling reduces amygdala activity and is discussed as incidental regulation, participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses. Satisfied inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task contrasts reported), I10 (group whole-brain maps with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (explicit emotion regulation) while participants view visual stimuli (negative images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraisal vs. Maintain and Reappraisal vs. Fixation), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and cluster-correction thresholds, and includes ROI analyses for the amygdala. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I5–I11) and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise vs React) and reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise > React) across three socio-emotional tasks. Two of the regulated stimulus types are visual (looming facial photographs and dynamic video clips of social criticism), which meet the review’s requirement for visual stimuli; although one task uses written autobiographical sentences, the presence of regulated visual stimuli suffices for inclusion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with thresholding and coordinates, and provides within-group and between-group task activation maps. Participant groups (SAD patients and healthy controls) are reported separately. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (reappraise vs attend) of visual sad images (IAPS and other pictures) in remitted MDD and control participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraise-sad > attend-sad), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported clusters/coordinates (tables/figures). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (increase, decrease, maintain) during recall of previously encoded visual images (IAPS). Methods report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8) with coordinates/tables and contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g., decrease>maintain, increase>maintain, conjunctions, phase-specific contrasts). Sample is healthy young adults and within-task contrasts are reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (mentalizing-reappraisal: up, down, look) during presentation of visual social stimuli (photos of proposers and monetary offers displayed on screen). The sample is healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., DOWN > LOOK, UP > LOOK, DOWN < LOOK < UP) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses with cluster-corrected thresholds and peak coordinates (tables/figures). Reporting meets the meta-analysis requirements for whole-brain voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, and includes explicit instructions to amplify/dampen emotion). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I11 and should be included.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (detach/experience) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Positive-Experience > Positive-Regulate; Negative-Regulate > Negative-Experience), trial-by-trial parametric analyses, and a group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis with MNI coordinates and cluster correction (tables/figures). Sample includes younger and older adults. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, sufficient for screening. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This full-text reports a task-based BOLD fMRI study that instructed participants to use cognitive reappraisal ("Reduce Emotion") vs maintain responses to negative images (I5, I6). Stimuli were visual IAPS pictures (I7). Participant groups include healthy controls and clinical groups with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Reappraise vs Baseline; Maintain vs Baseline; and task effects/interaction) and behavioral-fMRI relationships (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are presented with cluster thresholds and peak coordinates in Talairach space (I10), and results are reported in tables/figures/supplement (I11). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; reports whole-brain task activation maps; not only connectivity or ROI-only; includes within-group task effects; not an empathy/perspective-taking study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to label affect (an instructed strategy shown to function as incidental emotion regulation), using visual stimuli (photographs of faces). The sample includes GAD patients and healthy controls with group-level analyses. The paper reports within-task contrasts (emotion vs. fixation; affect vs. gender) and longitudinal regulation-related contrasts (pre–post changes, group-by-time interactions) and provides whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task effects, not an empathy/perspective-taking-only paradigm). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11.

Full text is complete. Met inclusion: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: facial images), I8 (eligible sample: healthy adults), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates), I11 (results reported clearly in text/tables). Not met: I6 — the task did NOT instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraise, down-regulate, accept). Instead, the Cued Emotional Conflict Task required cognitive control/response mapping (respond to actual vs. opposite emotion) and the study correlated habitual ERQ scores with task activation; participants were not instructed to regulate their emotional responses in-scanner. I9 — there is no within-task contrast that reflects an instructed emotion-regulation condition (e.g., “reappraise > look”, “down-regulate > maintain”) nor a standard unregulated viewing contrast of emotion versus baseline that maps onto passive viewing; the reported contrasts index cognitive control/conflict (opposite vs actual) rather than an explicit regulation instruction. Therefore the study does not satisfy the core requirement (I6) and is excluded.

The full text meets all required inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study that uses instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal: downregulate and upregulate) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The sample (healthy participants; genotype groups reported) is acceptable, and the paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (downregulate > look, upregulate > look, negative > neutral). Group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates and cluster thresholds in standard space, satisfying whole-brain evidence. The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-without-regulation) are met.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with an instructed reappraisal/perspective-taking regulation strategy (meets I5, I6), includes an appropriate sample (I8), reports within-task regulation-related contrasts (I9) and presents group-level whole-brain analyses/coordinates (I10, I11), it does NOT meet the required stimulus modality criterion: the emotional content consists of monetary decision outcomes and numeric gamble displays rather than visual emotional stimuli (e.g., IAPS images, faces, or film/video). Therefore inclusion criterion I7 (visual emotional stimuli) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs participants to regulate emotional responses (explicit up-regulation via instructed imitation, IMT, and down-regulation via expressive suppression, eSUP) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (dynamic face video clips). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (IMT > eSUP, IMT > GND, eSUP > IMT, etc.) and conducts group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with coordinates and cluster reporting. The sample (20 healthy adults) is acceptable, and the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-task effects, not an empathy task without regulation). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) during an fMRI Ultimatum Game and during IAPS training, fulfilling the review focus on instructed emotion regulation. Stimuli are visual (IAPS pictures in training and photographs of proposers/faces during the task). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Down > Look, Down < Look < Up, regulated decisions contrasts) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. Participant sample is healthy adults and methods/results/discussion are fully presented. No exclusion criteria (ROIs-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or perspective-taking without regulation) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI experiment that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) and also includes a placebo regulation condition. Visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures) were used. The sample comprises healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g. RU–CUR, PU–CUP and related conjunction/subtraction contrasts) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates and tables/figures in standard space. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, non-empirical paper, or empathy-only perspective tasks) are met. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study using an instructed cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task (regulate vs. look) with visual stimuli (IAPS photographs). It reports within-task contrasts for emotional reactivity (negative > neutral) and reappraisal (regulate negative > look negative) with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and MNI peak coordinates (whole-brain FWE correction for regulate>look). Sample and analyses meet inclusion requirements. The full text is complete (background, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and not an empathy without regulation task).

Exclusion E4 applies: the study reports primarily ROI/mask-based voxelwise analyses (a priori ROIs: left/right amygdala and insula; exploratory larger ROI mask) and does not present a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map in standard space. Consequently inclusion criterion I10 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. The study does satisfy: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed implicit emotion-regulation paradigm via attend/ignore instructions qualifies as instructed cognitive control), I7 (visual stimuli—faces and houses), I8 (sample reported; clinical group with controls), and I9 (within-task contrasts related to regulation/attention: attend vs ignore fearful faces and emotion×attention interactions). Because I10 is not met and E4 is triggered (ONLY ROI/mask results), the study is excluded from the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation (reappraise and distract) while participants view sad images (visual stimuli). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., Sad-Reappraise > Sad-View, Sad-Distract > Sad-View) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise mixed-effects analyses in MNI space with tables/figures of cluster results. The sample and analyses meet eligibility and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-only, not empathy-without-regulation). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; full text appears complete.

This article meets all inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs explicit emotion regulation strategies including cognitive reappraisal and distraction (I6). The emotional stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). The sample includes remitted MDD patients and healthy controls with group-level results reported (I8). Analyses include within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraisal vs. view; distraction vs. view) and viewing contrasts (I9). The paper reports group-level activation peaks in standard (MNI) space (e.g., amygdala coordinates) and thresholding information, consistent with whole-brain/voxelwise reporting (I10,I11). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal) using visual stimuli (IAPS images and facial displays) in an appropriate adult sample and reports within-task contrasts (Look vs Decrease; Match vs Label). However, all activation effects are reported using ROI-based analyses (amygdala ROIs) and PPI connectivity analyses restricted to anatomically defined IFG masks. The paper does not present any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (analyses were mask-restricted), so it fails inclusion criterion I10 and (by implication) I11. This violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI / small-volume-corrected results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This article meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using instructed cognitive reappraisal (I6) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures; I7). The sample is healthy adults (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. Reappraise > Attend; Reappraise negative > Attend negative; Attend negative > Reappraise negative) (I9). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates in MNI space and described in the text and figures (I10, I11). The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided and complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, not an empathy-only paradigm).

This paper is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (decrease) versus look conditions using visual stimuli (IAPS and child-friendly pictures). The sample includes ages 10–22 (children, adolescents, young adults). The manuscript reports within-task contrasts of interest (decrease negative > look negative; look negative > look neutral), and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and peak coordinates (tables/supplementary material). The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study with explicit instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal REAP and suppression ESUP) and a natural viewing condition. Emotional stimuli are visual static images (IAPS and photos) with social/nonsocial categories. Sample includes 19 healthy adults. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., social pleasant vs nonsocial pleasant; effects during NAT, REAP, ESUP) and whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with reported peak coordinates and SPM maps. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I11) and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full article reports an fMRI task with instructed cognitive reappraisal (distancing) during anticipation of visual reward cues (coins). Methods and analyses include within-task regulation contrasts (regulate > permit and interactions), whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and appropriate correction, and task-based design. Sample is healthy adults. All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply; full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: distancing reappraisal), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task reappraisal contrasts reported, e.g., R–NR), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported MNI peak coordinates), I11 (results reported in text/tables/figures). This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (sad and neutral film clips) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (Sad > Neutral). Whole-brain group-level analyses are reported with peak coordinates in standard space, and the full article includes methods, results, and discussion. The study therefore meets the review’s scope (studies of viewing visual emotional stimuli without regulation) and satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which children/adolescents were instructed to regulate emotional responses (cognitive reappraisal-style strategies: ‘pretend it’s fake’ or ‘pretend it’s right in front of you’) while viewing visual disgust-inducing images (IAPS and in-house images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (decrease-gross > look-gross; increase-gross > look-gross) and unregulated viewing (look-gross > look-neutral). Group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (with cluster thresholds and Talairach coordinates). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study (N=30) that explicitly instructs emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and distraction) during presentation of visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (reappraisal > view; distraction > view; reappraisal vs distraction), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FDR correction, and tables/figures with peak coordinates. Sample is healthy adults and the full text contains methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) during presentation of visual emotional images (IAPS and Internet pictures).
